chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Mundhir al-Zabbal, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you have a dirham, buy wheat with it, for the loss (of value) is in the flour.

key_terms.الْمَحْق: Annihilation, loss, or depreciation of value.
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A silver coin used as currency.

ai.seo_question: Why is it better to buy wheat than flour according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises purchasing raw wheat over processed flour to preserve value, as the milling process incurs greater loss (al-mahq) through waste and spoilage. This hadith, found in al-Kafi’s chapter on the merits of foodstuffs, reflects the economic prudence of the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing the preservation of sustenance (rizq) and minimizing waste in daily transactions. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical wisdom in trade, linking material stewardship to spiritual responsibility.
